name: Being.Marketing: Your Existential Coach
oneLine: A quiet companion for rest from anxious purpose-hunting, tasks, and roles.
what: A quiet companion for rest from anxious purpose-hunting, tasks, and roles, and a clear mirror for your inner language — the listing invites you to lay down a concern or identity like a stone. It is offered two ways: as a custom ChatGPT, or reached from the web without logging in to ChatGPT, which the page describes as being for ultimate privacy. The page also says your dialogue can seed your GPT's training data or AI prompt to share as a custom ChatGPT, so others can quietly sit beside it as well. It is published and listed free on the being.marketing storefront.
built: Custom ChatGPT — offered as the "Custom ChatGPT" option on the listing
A web version usable without a ChatGPT login — the "W/o login to ChatGPT" option, described on the page as being for ultimate privacy
Published through a Gumroad storefront served on the being.marketing custom domain (product permalink /l/being)
status: Live — published and listed at $0 (pay-what-you-want enabled, no suggested price) on being.marketing

brandTypography.intent: The brand is written as the word "Being." followed by the word "Marketing" struck through — the strikethrough crosses out "Marketing", leaving "Being." standing.
brandTypography.renderWith: Real markup, e.g. Being.<s>Marketing</s> or a CSS line-through span, with the accessible text reading "Being.Marketing".
brandTypography.howTheLiveSiteDoesIt: Not with markup. On the product page the title is built from Unicode look-alikes: "Being." is plain ASCII, and each letter of "Marketing" is a Mathematical Sans-Serif letter (U+1D5AC, U+1D5BA, U+1D5CB, U+1D5C4, U+1D5BE, U+1D5CD, U+1D5C2, U+1D5C7, U+1D5C0) each followed by U+0336 COMBINING LONG STROKE OVERLAY to fake the strike.
brandTypography.doesLiveSiteRenderItThatWay: Only via that Unicode hack, and only in the product's own title. The front page at https://being.marketing sets its own <title> and profile name as the plain ASCII "Being.Marketing" (its og:title is "Subscribe to Being.Marketing on Gumroad"), but the product tile for this GPT on that front page carries the same struck Unicode name as the product page. The product page's own schema.org brand name is the plain "Being.Marketing".
brandTypography.notes: "Being." is plain ASCII everywhere it was checked, on both pages; only "Marketing" is faked. The struck Unicode form is what breaks screen readers and search, which is why it is described here rather than pasted.

unverifiedClaims: No launch, publish, or update date appears on either page, so fetchedAt and any date for this build are null — do not state when it shipped.
No usage, adoption, download, or sales figures are given. The product page reports 0 ratings and no sales count; do not imply traction.
The pages never name the underlying model or version, and never describe the system prompt, instructions, or knowledge files behind the GPT.
The pages do not say what the no-login web version actually runs on, or how its "ultimate privacy" is achieved — that phrase is the page's claim, not a verified property.
Neither page links to chatgpt.com or the OpenAI GPT Store, so there is no evidence of a public GPT Store listing or a direct chat link.
"Existential Coach" is the product's own title. Neither page claims therapy, counselling, clinical benefit, or any credential — do not add one, and do not describe it as a mental-health service.
The front page never mentions this GPT in prose — it appears only as one product tile in an "AI development" section, so there is no front-page narrative about it to quote.

The front-page bio carries the owner's own agency claims ("20+ yrs of experience in IT, marketing and psychology", "the past eight years", "conversion rate from leads to B2B contracts exceeds 3%"). Those are about the agency, not about this GPT, and are unaudited — do not attach them to this build.
How the owner himself types the brand was not sourced — only the two rendered pages were checked, so nothing here describes his own typing, and "Being." is plain ASCII in both.
notes:
PUBLISH URL: https://being.marketing (the root domain), per the site owner's explicit instruction. The description was read from the product page https://being.marketing/l/being, which is that page's own canonical URL — use it as the source, not as the link.

Fetch method: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 on both URLs (both the bare and trailing-slash variants). curl with a normal browser user-agent returned HTTP 200, and every field above comes from that retrieved HTML — the product page's meta description, og tags, schema.org Product block, and the embedded Inertia page props. Nothing here is inferred.

The page's description verbatim: "A quiet companion for rest from anxious purpose-hunting, tasks, and roles. A clear mirror for your inner language. Lay down a concern or identity like a stone. Your dialogue can also seed your  GPT ’s training data or AI prompt to share as a custom ChatGPT. So others can quietly sit beside it as well." The two listed options verbatim: "W/o login to ChatGPT" — "Access Being.Marketing from web for ultimate privacy"; and "Custom ChatGPT" — "Being.Marketing as a custom ChatGPT". Both are $0. (Brand name de-styled here; see brandTypography.)

Platform: the site is a Gumroad seller profile on a custom domain (seller "Being.Marketing", Gumroad subdomain linked.gumroad.com, product permalink adzva, native_type digital, is_published true, availability InStock).

This GPT sits in the section headed "AI development: anything you ever wanted to be created in digital world, either for your business or as a pet project", alongside "FREE consultation: Replit Vibe Coding" ($0), "GPT to Share Your Unique Life Story" ($7), and "Free Instant launch of Your Google Ad Grant" ($0). A second section headed "LinkedIn Growth Hacking: never spam or cold outreach, reasonable AI and automations, 100% safe for your account" lists "Marketing Q/A" ($200), "Top Voice AI: Chat with AIs of Top Influencers" ($0), and "LinkedIn Organic Traffic for Your Profiles or Pages" ($0). Product prices are set in USD (currency_code "usd" on every tile); the storefront renders them in the visitor's local currency (this fetch, from Czechia, returned display_mode "buyer_local" and czk), so the USD figures above are the product prices, not necessarily what a given visitor sees.
